chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa — all of them from Muawiya ibn Ammar who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When the water reaches the measure of a kurr, nothing can make it impure.

key_terms.طَهَارَة: Ritual purity (taharah) — the state being protected by this ruling
key_terms.كُرّ: A unit of volume measurement used in Islamic law; classically defined as approximately 36 spans (shibr) cubed or roughly 384-425 litres. Water reaching this quantity cannot be made ritually impure.
key_terms.يُنَجِّسْهُ: To make ritually impure (najis); the verb form of najasah (ritual impurity). This is a technical term in Islamic jurisprudence.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on kurr water in Islamic jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the fundamental jurisprudential ruling on water purity: a large body of water reaching the quantity known as a 'kurr' (approximately 384 litres by classical estimation) cannot be rendered ritually impure by contact with a najis substance. This ruling forms the cornerstone of Islamic water purity law and is transmitted through a highly reliable chain of narrators from the major schools of Shia hadith transmission in Kufa, Basra, and Nishapur.
